chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Five people do not lead the people in prayer under any circumstances: the leper, the one with vitiligo, the madman, the son of fornication, and the Bedouin.

key_terms.يَؤُمُّونَ: lead in prayer / serve as imam

ai.seo_question: Who are the five people who cannot lead prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this chain to establish the five categories permanently disqualified from leading congregational prayer, emphasizing that these disqualifications are inherent rather than situational. The inclusion of the 'son of fornication' (walad al-zina) and the 'Bedouin' (al-Arabi) highlights specific Shia jurisprudential views on lineage and social refinement (adab) as criteria for spiritual leadership, distinguishing them from mere ritual purity.
